parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A circular metal disc spins horizontally about a vertical axis, as shown in Fig. 1.1.

[[fig:f1]]

A piece of modelling clay is attached to the disc.

For the instant when the piece of modelling clay is in the position shown, draw on Fig. 1.1:
parts.text: an arrow, labelled *V*, showing the direction of the velocity of the modelling clay

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: an arrow, labelled *A*, showing the direction of the acceleration of the modelling clay

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead:
The metal disc in Fig. 1.1 has a radius of 9.3 cm.
The centre of gravity of the modelling clay is 1.2 cm from the rim of the disc and moves with a speed of 0.68 m s⁻¹.
parts.text: Calculate the angular speed *ω* of the disc.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the acceleration *a* of the centre of gravity of the modelling clay.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
A second piece of modelling clay is attached to the disc in the position shown in Fig. 1.2.

[[fig:f2]]

The second piece of modelling clay has a larger mass than the first piece.

By placing one tick (✓) in each row, complete Table 1.1 to show how the quantities indicated compare for the two pieces of modelling clay.
